gloss: to wrap a bandage; to bandage

definitions.gloss: to wrap a bandage; to bandage
definitions.explanation: To wind a bandage around a wound or injured body part.

examples.japanese: {傷口|きずぐち}に{包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}く。
examples.english: To wrap a bandage around the wound.

examples.japanese: {看護師|かんごし}が{手首|てくび}に{包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}いてくれた。
examples.english: The nurse wrapped a bandage around my wrist.

examples.japanese: {応急手当|おうきゅうてあて}として、{清潔|せいけつ}な{布|ぬの}がなかったので、ハンカチで{代用|だいよう}して{包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}いた。
examples.english: As first aid, since there was no clean cloth available, I used a handkerchief as a substitute and wrapped it as a bandage.

notes:
The standard expression for applying a bandage in Japanese. {巻|ま}く (to wind, to wrap) is the most natural verb to use with {包帯|ほうたい} (bandage), reflecting the winding motion of wrapping a bandage around a body part.

For removing a bandage, use {包帯|ほうたい}を{外|はず}す (to remove a bandage) or {包帯|ほうたい}を{取|と}る (to take off a bandage).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {包帯|ほうたい}をきつく{巻|ま}く: to wrap a bandage tightly
- {包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}き{直|なお}す: to rewrap a bandage
- {腕|うで}に{包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}く: to bandage an arm
- {頭|あたま}に{包帯|ほうたい}を{巻|ま}く: to wrap a bandage around the head

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絆創膏|ばんそうこう}を{貼|は}る: to put on a bandage/plaster — for small wounds, using adhesive bandages
- {手当|てあて}をする: to give first aid — broader term for treating an injury
- {包帯|ほうたい}を{外|はず}す: to remove a bandage — the opposite action
